runner.text:
**Brief for the coach — what this check found**

This pass was housekeeping, not programming. I was confirming where the plate-loading helper links live in the athlete's published pages and whether everything is saved and published. Nothing here changes a load, set, rep range, or date, and there are no warnings and no proposed changes for the athlete to agree to.

**Where the plate-loading links appear**

The athlete's home-kit routine pages each carry a "set up the home kit" link near the top that opens the plate-loading tool pre-filled with their home inventory. That link is present on seven routines: Sunday deadlift, Monday overhead press, Wednesday pull-up, Friday squat, Saturday bench, the conditioning circuit, and the daily hang. Every one of them has it in the same spot, so the athlete will see it consistently.

Below those, the individual exercise lines carry "load it" links that open the tool already set to a specific weight. The weights currently published are:

- Barbell at 140.5 lb with collar clamps
- Barbell at 55.5 lb with collar clamps
- Dumbbell at 32.5 lb with standard screw collars
- Dumbbell at 20 lb with standard screw collars (this one appears on two separate lines)
- Dumbbell at 5 lb with no collars
- Kettlebell at 40 lb with standard screw collars

Those are the figures the athlete will be shown when they tap through; if any look wrong to you, tell me which and I can find the routine line that produces it.

**The athlete's profile page**

The athlete page mentions the plate-loading tool once, on a single line describing how the home kit is organised: barbell, dumbbell, kettlebell, a leg attachment, and a weighted vest. That is just the equipment map, not any training numbers.

**Save and publish status**

The most recent saved change to the athlete page was the last coach publish, and there is nothing unsaved anywhere in the pages area. The pages are set up to publish to the athlete's training site hosted on GitHub. The pages area contains the athlete profile, the check-ins, the progress page, the routines, and the current week's page.

**Bottom line**

Everything the athlete sees is saved and published, the plate-loading links are in place on all seven home-kit routines, and no action or agreement is needed from the athlete right now.

first.text:
My mistake — I sent you to the wrong page. Your profile page only describes the home kit; it doesn't carry the setup link.

The link you want is on each of your home-kit routine pages, not the profile. Open any of them on your phone — Sunday deadlift, Monday overhead press, Wednesday pull-up, Friday squat, Saturday bench, the conditioning circuit, or the daily hang — and near the top you'll see "set up the home kit." Tap that once and it opens the plate-loading tool with your barbell, dumbbell, kettlebell and the rest already filled in. Save it there and you're done.

After that, each exercise line on those routine pages has a "load it" link that opens the tool already set to that day's weight, so you won't need the long link again.

If you open a routine page and still don't see "set up the home kit" near the top, tell me which one and I'll check it.
